minuteOfHour.description: Minute past every hour an HOURLY rule is checked, 0 to 59.

weekday.description: Run day of a weekly or biweekly rule.

subaccountId.description: Public subaccount ID the rule belongs to; zero for the root account.

limit.description: Maximum number of runs to return: 0 means 20, at most 100.

pageToken.description: Opaque, exclusive, keyset-backed cursor from a previous response, bound to the caller's account or subaccount and the newest-first run_seq order. Empty for the first page.

subaccountId.description: Public subaccount ID; omit for the root account.

nextPageToken.description: Cursor for the next page. Empty when no more results exist.

runs.description: Runs ordered by run_seq, newest first.

conversions.description: Conversions into the rule's payout asset, ordered by source_asset_id; empty for an in-kind rule.

amount.description: Amount the conversion spends, as a decimal string in whole units of the source asset.

executedAmount.description: Source asset spent, settled, as a decimal string in whole units.

execution.description: Market or TWAP; unset when the asset was not converted.

durationMs.description: Total execution duration in milliseconds, from 60000 (1 minute) to 3600000 (60 minutes). The duration starts when execution starts.

sliceIntervalMs.description: Interval between slices in milliseconds, from 10000 (10 seconds) up to duration_ms. The slice count is duration_ms / slice_interval_ms, rounded up.

isTerminal.description: Whether the conversion is over: its Swap is terminal, or it was skipped.

fee.description: Fee the leg paid in the asset it received, as a decimal string in whole units.

feeAssetId.description: Asset the leg's fee was charged in: the asset it received.

leg.description: Route leg: 0, or 1 for a route's second leg.

received.description: Asset the leg received after its fee, as a decimal string in whole units.

side.description: Whether the leg bought or sold the market's base asset.

spent.description: Asset the leg spent, as a decimal string in whole units.

symbolId.description: Spot market the leg traded on.

reason.description: Why a terminal Swap did not trade its whole amount; absent when it did or when the asset was not converted.

receivedAmount.description: Payout asset received after fees, as a decimal string in whole units.

skipReason.description: Why the asset was not converted (route_unsupported, below_minimum, above_maximum, conversion_unavailable, price_unavailable, conversion_refused, rule_superseded or policy_denied); empty otherwise. Its balance stays on the account.

status.description: Where the Swap stands; absent when the asset was not converted (skipReason says why).

swapId.description: The Swap that converts the asset; absent when the asset was not converted.

unspentAmount.description: Source asset left on the account, as a decimal string in whole units.

finishedAt.description: When the run ended; unset while it is in progress.

reason.description: Machine-readable reason for a skipped run: nothing_to_pay, price_unavailable (an asset was not paid because no current price valued it) or rule_superseded; empty otherwise.

ruleVersion.description: The rule version the run executes.

runSeq.description: The account's run number, increasing by one per run.

scheduledFor.description: The scheduled slot the run belongs to.

steps.description: One step per destination of the rule version, ordered by asset_id. Empty while the run is planned.

amount.description: What the step pays, as a decimal string in whole units of the asset; '0' when skipped.

assetId.description: Ledger asset paid.

available.description: The account's available balance of the asset when the run started, as a decimal string in whole units of the asset.

destinationAddress.description: Canonical destination address.

intentId.description: Withdraw intent identifier once the withdrawal is accepted; follows the same lifecycle as a user withdrawal.

networkFee.description: The network fee charged on the withdrawal, as a decimal string in whole units of the asset. Once it completed, the destination received amount minus this fee; once Zipper rejected it or its execution failed, the fee Zipper kept, which is not refunded. Absent until the step is final, when it was skipped or failed before it reached Zipper, and when the fee was not reported.

reason.description: Machine-readable reason for a skipped or failed step, such as below_minimum, price_unavailable (the rule has a USD minimum and no current price valued the asset; the funds stay for a later run), rule_superseded, destination_not_whitelisted, destination_cooling_down (a broker vault's destination added to its external withdraw whitelist less than 24 hours ago; the funds stay for a later run), route_suspended (withdrawals of the asset to the destination network are suspended, as its withdrawal_status SUSPENDED in the deposit and withdraw config shows; the funds stay for a later run), supply_unavailable (the destination route's supply_status in the deposit and withdraw config is MISSING or STALE; the funds stay for a later run), authority_revoked, gateway_capacity_insufficient (the funds stay for a later run), withdrawals_disabled (the environment does not allow withdrawals; the funds stay on the account), withdrawal_released or withdrawal_failed; empty otherwise.

txHash.description: Destination-network transaction hash, set once Zipper committed the withdrawal's destination transaction and empty before. On a completed step it is the delivery. When the withdrawal's execution failed after that commit, the step fails with withdrawal_failed and keeps this hash: the funds were not returned to the account, and the bridge operator reviews the withdrawal.

valueUsd.description: USD value of the payable amount when the run started, as a decimal string in whole USD; absent when the rule has no USD minimum or no current price was available.

subaccountId.description: Public subaccount ID; omit for the root account.

assets.description: One entry per destination of the rule, then per other asset with a positive balance, ordered by asset_id. Empty when the account has no rule or the rule is paused.

assetId.description: Ledger asset.

available.description: The account's available balance of the asset now, as a decimal string in whole units of the asset.

conversion.description: Set on an asset the rule converts into its payout asset: what converting its whole available balance is quoted to deliver now. Such an asset pays nothing in kind (payable_e18 zero); its hold_reason is converts, or why it would stay on the account.

execution.description: How the run would execute the conversion: market, or TWAP over the rule's conversion duration when its USD value exceeds 10,000 or its price impact exceeds 0.5%. durationMs.description: Total execution duration in milliseconds, from 60000 (1 minute) to 3600000 (60 minutes). The duration starts when execution starts.

sliceIntervalMs.description: Interval between slices in milliseconds, from 10000 (10 seconds) up to duration_ms. The slice count is duration_ms / slice_interval_ms, rounded up.

expectedAmountOut.description: Expected payout asset after every leg's fee, as a decimal string in whole units, estimated from the whole amount at the current book depth; a TWAP's slices execute at the prices of their own time.

minAmountOut.description: Least payout asset the conversion accepts, as a decimal string in whole units: the expected amount less the 1% slippage protection, estimated the same way.

priceImpactBps.description: Quoted price impact of the whole amount, in basis points.

skipReason.description: Why the asset would not be converted now (route_unsupported, below_minimum, above_maximum, conversion_unavailable, price_unavailable); empty when it would. Its balance stays on the account.

destinationAddress.description: Canonical destination address; absent when the rule has no destination for the asset.

destinationChainId.description: External destination chain identifier; absent when the rule has no destination for the asset.

heldBack.description: What would stay on the account, as a decimal string in whole units of the asset: available minus payable.

holdReason.description: Why held_back_e18 stays, or why nothing pays: below_minimum (below minimum_e18 or the rule's min_usd_value_e18), price_unavailable (the rule has a USD minimum and no current price values the asset), no_destination (the rule pays no destination for the asset), destination_cooling_down (a broker vault pays a destination only once it has been on the vault's external withdraw whitelist for 24 hours; see payable_from), above_max (the balance above max_amount_e18 stays), dust (less than one whole on-chain unit stays) or, on a rule with a payout asset, converts (the asset is converted into the payout asset instead; see conversion) or why it would not be converted (see conversion.skip_reason); empty when the whole balance pays.

minimum.description: The least one payout of the asset pays, as a decimal string in whole units of the asset: the destination's minAmount, or its minFloor when that is higher and known now. Absent when the rule has no destination for the asset.

payable.description: What the run would pay, as a decimal string in whole units of the asset; '0' when the asset holds. The network fee is taken out of it on the way.

pricedAt.description: When the price behind value_usd_e18 was observed; unset with it.

publishedAt.description: Publication time of the post in this environment. For a release post, the time its release went live here, the same value as this environment's live_at in environments (releases that went live together share it), or the time the post was first published while the release is still pending here. It follows that live_at, without a new revision: it changes when the release goes live here and whenever that live_at changes later. For other posts, the time of first publication. It never changes when the post is republished. Post lists are ordered by it, newest first, then by release version descending at equal times.

releaseVersion.description: Release the post announces, for example "0.92.9". Omitted for posts that do not announce one release. postOnlyReserveFeeRatePercent.description: Fee rate a new post-only limit order on this market reserves its fee at when the fee is paid in the quote asset, encoded as a non-negative base-10 percentage string without a percent sign, between 0 and 100 inclusive: the highest maker rate of every VIP tier under the fee schedule in force on this market, as reserve_fee_rate_percent describes.

reserveFeeRatePercent.description: Fee rate a new order on this market reserves its fee at when the fee is paid in the quote asset, encoded as a non-negative base-10 percentage string without a percent sign, between 0 and 100 inclusive. It is the highest maker or taker rate of every VIP tier under the fee schedule in force on this market, so it is at least the effective rates and discounts never lower it. A buy limit order that pays its fee in the quote asset reserves N + F, computed in units of 10^-18 of the quote asset whatever the quote asset's own decimals: N is its price times its quantity rounded up to 10^-18, and F is N times this rate rounded up to 10^-18. It has sufficient quote balance when N + F is at most the available quote balance, compared in the same 10^-18 units; other order validation and market limits still apply. A post-only limit order reserves at post_only_reserve_fee_rate_percent instead. An order that can only take, a market order or an IOC or FOK limit order such as a buy sized by a quote amount, fixes its fee cap when it is accepted: the lower of this rate and taker_fee_rate_percent in force then. A fixed-quantity buy among them that pays its fee in the quote asset reserves its fee at that cap; a buy sized by a quote amount holds its whole budget, which a lower cap lets buy more. A standalone stop-loss, take-profit or trailing stop whose order can only take fixes the cap when the stop is created, and each slice of a TWAP whose slices can only take when that slice is placed. Take-profit and stop-loss orders attached to an order or paired in an OCO, and orders that can rest, are capped at this rate, a post-only one at post_only_reserve_fee_rate_percent. Rates read before an order is sent are an estimate: a VIP tier or fee policy change before the order is accepted changes them. Each fill is charged the rate of the VIP tier and fee policy current when the fill is settled, never above the order's cap: in the quote asset on the fill's notional, or for a buy paying its fee in the base asset, in base on the quantity it receives. The cap is an upper bound on every fill, not a fixed rate: a VIP tier change after the order is accepted can move a later fill's rate up or down within it, but never above it. The rest of the reserve is released as the order fills or ends.

minSellPrice.description: The lowest sell limit price admitted, inclusive, as a decimal string. Present only when state is ACTIVE.

parameters.description: The band's settings, as GetSpotConfig returns them. Absent when the state is OFF, or when the settings in effect cannot be expressed exactly in basis points and milliseconds; the limits above are authoritative either way.

lowerBps.description: How far below the reference price a sell may be priced or trade, in basis points (1 bp = 0.01%). The lower limit is the reference price times (1 - lower_bps / 10000), rounded up to the tick size.

referenceWindowMs.description: How long the reference price stays fixed before it can move to a newer trade, in milliseconds. Zero moves it with every order.

upperBps.description: How far above the reference price a buy may be priced or trade, in basis points. The upper limit is the reference price times (1 + upper_bps / 10000), rounded down to the tick size.

reanchorEligibleAt.description: From when the next order operation on the pair may move the reference price. Nothing moves at that time by itself. Present when state is ACTIVE or EMPTY.

reanchorPending.description: True when a trade newer than the reference price is waiting: once the re-anchor eligibility time has passed, the next order operation moves the reference to it, unless the index price moves it instead. False does not promise that the band stays: a move to the index price needs no trade.

referencePrice.description: The band's reference price as a decimal string in quote asset units per base asset unit, for example '61000.25'. Present when state is ACTIVE or EMPTY.

referenceSource.description: Where the reference price came from. REFERENCE_SOURCE_UNSPECIFIED when the state is OFF or UNKNOWN.

symbol.description: The pair's symbol, for example BTC-USDT.

updateId.description: Increases with each band update within an epoch, and may increase without one, as an unsigned 64-bit decimal string. Compare it only within one epoch: a greater value is newer.

updatedAt.description: When the band last changed: its first setting, OFF included, a change of its settings, or a move of its reference price, to the same price included.

validUntil.description: asOf plus 5 seconds. After it, treat the band as unknown and read it again.

assets.description: Assets ordered by asset code in ascending alphabetical order.

includedInEquity.description: Counted in the account's total equity. When false, balances of this asset are still reported but carry no value in total equity. Always set; treat an absent value as unknown, never as false.

ledgerId.description: Stable numeric asset id used by account, balance, and order APIs.

marketDataVolumeScale.description: Integer scale for public candle and market-overview base volume (0..18).

quantityDisplayDecimals.description: Suggested decimal precision for displaying user-facing asset amounts.

quantityScale.description: Decimal scale (0..18) for this asset's order quantities and other fields that explicitly reference quantity_scale. A scale of 8 represents one whole asset as 100000000 in those fields. Account balance amounts use fixed 18-decimal units independently of this value.

maxOpenOrdersTotal.description: The venue's default limit on resting orders a typical account may hold across all pairs together: good-till-cancelled and good-till-date orders that have not ended. Immediate-or-cancel, fill-or-kill and market orders never count, and a replaced order keeps its place. An order past it is rejected with MAX_OPEN_ORDERS_TOTAL. Each pair's own limit is PairConfig.max_open_orders_per_pair. An account may have a lower limit of its own; that is not part of this public configuration and would be returned by an account-scoped read.

pairs.description: Pairs ordered by symbol in ascending alphabetical order.

allowBuyFeeFromBase.description: Whether BUY order fees may be paid from the base asset instead of the spent quote asset when the order request selects the base fee asset.

baseAsset.description: Base asset code. For BTC-USDT, this is "BTC".

baseQuantityScale.description: Quantity scale for base-asset amounts in this pair.

defaultMarketSlippageBpsBuy.description: Default MARKET order slippage cap for BUY orders, in basis points (1 bp = 0.01%). A request-level slippage setting can override this value.

defaultMarketSlippageBpsSell.description: Default MARKET order slippage cap for SELL orders, in basis points (1 bp = 0.01%). A request-level slippage setting can override this value.

delistingAt.description: Scheduled delisting timestamp. When unset, the pair has no explicit delisting time.

listingAt.description: Scheduled listing timestamp. When unset, the pair has no explicit future listing time.

marketdata.description: Market-data display settings for this pair.

orderbookPriceBuckets.description: Suggested order book aggregation bucket sizes in quote-asset price units, e.g. 0.01, 0.1, 1, or 10.

maxClientRefDriftBps.description: Maximum allowed drift between client reference price and server reference price for MARKET orders, in basis points (1 bp = 0.01%), when client reference pricing is used.

maxLimitQtyBase.description: Largest quantity of one limit order, as a decimal string in base-asset units. A replace is checked on its new total less the quantity already filled. An order above it is rejected with MAX_QTY. Absent when the pair has no maximum.

maxMarketNotionalQuote.description: Additional maximum notional for market orders as a decimal string in quote-asset units. Base-sized market orders are valued at the buy protection price or the sell reference price before slippage, without rounding. For quote-sized market buys, the entire all-in maximum quote debit must also fit this maximum, and for quote-sized market sells the entire quote proceeds target. Exceeding it returns MAX_NOTIONAL. Absent when no maximum is configured.

maxMarketQtyBase.description: Largest quantity of one market order, as a decimal string in base-asset units. A market order sized by quote amount is checked once converted to base. An order above it is rejected with MAX_QTY. Absent when the pair has no maximum.

maxOpenOrdersPerPair.description: The venue's default limit on resting orders a typical account may hold on this pair at once: good-till-cancelled and good-till-date orders that have not ended. Immediate-or-cancel, fill-or-kill and market orders never count, and a replaced order keeps its place. An order past it is rejected with MAX_OPEN_ORDERS_PER_PAIR. An account may have a lower limit of its own; that is not part of this public configuration and would be returned by an account-scoped read.

maxOrderNotionalQuote.description: Maximum per-order notional as a decimal string in quote-asset units. Base-sized orders are checked using quantity times limit price, or market protection price, without rounding. For quote-sized buys, the entire all-in maximum quote debit must also fit this maximum, and for quote-sized sells the entire quote proceeds target. Exceeding it returns MAX_NOTIONAL. Absent when no maximum is configured.

minNotionalQuote.description: Minimum order notional as a decimal string in quote-asset units.

minQtyBase.description: Minimum order quantity as a decimal string in base-asset units.

priceBand.description: The pair's price band. Absent when the pair has none.

lowerBps.description: How far below the reference price a sell may be priced or trade, in basis points (1 bp = 0.01%). The lower limit is the reference price times (1 - lower_bps / 10000), rounded up to the tick size.

referenceWindowMs.description: How long the reference price stays fixed before it can move to a newer trade, in milliseconds. Zero moves it with every order.

upperBps.description: How far above the reference price a buy may be priced or trade, in basis points. The upper limit is the reference price times (1 + upper_bps / 10000), rounded down to the tick size.

quoteAsset.description: Quote asset code. For BTC-USDT, this is "USDT".

quoteQuantityScale.description: Quantity scale for quote-asset amounts in this pair.

referencePriceScale.description: Integer scale for composite reference prices in candle responses (0..18). Primary market and execution prices use the fixed scale 9.

stepSize.description: Minimum allowed quantity increment as a decimal string in base-asset units.

symbolId.description: Stable numeric pair id used by low-latency ConnectRPC requests and streams.

tickSize.description: Minimum allowed price increment as a decimal string in quote-asset units. Prices use 9 decimal places in scaled integer fields; for example "0.01" means orders must be priced in 0.01 quote-asset increments.

tsSec.description: Snapshot generation timestamp, in seconds since the Unix epoch (UTC).

completeThroughTradeId.description: With afterTradeId only: every trade with matchId at or below it exists and is returned by this endpoint.

epochEnds.description: Set only with after_trade_id. Every epoch whose last trade (or, for an epoch without trades, its start) lies between after_trade_id and next_after_trade_id, both inclusive, ascending by epoch. A page that ends exactly on an epoch's last trade is followed by a page that still reports that epoch's end.

lastTradeId.description: match_id of the epoch's last trade; (epoch-1) * 2^40 when the epoch ended without trades.

nextAfterTradeId.description: With afterTradeId only: the afterTradeId of the next call. It never moves backwards; equal to the request's afterTradeId when nothing newer is available yet.

nextPageToken.description: Opaque cursor for the next page. Empty when no more results exist, and always empty with after_trade_id.

trades.description: Trades ordered newest-first by execution timestamp, with match_id as a tie-breaker; with after_trade_id, ascending by match_id.

executedAt.description: Trade execution timestamp, in nanoseconds since the Unix epoch (UTC).

matchId.description: Stable trade id within the symbol, suitable for pagination and de-duplication.

price.description: Trade price as a decimal string in quote asset units per base asset unit, for example '61000.25'.

qty.description: Traded quantity as a decimal string in base asset units, for example '0.001'.

side.description: True when the taker/aggressor bought the base asset; false when the taker/aggressor sold the base asset.

symbol.description: Stable numeric pair id from GetSpotConfig.

assetInfo.description: Complete finite result, ordered by ascending asset_id. No pagination.

assetId.description: Numeric asset ID, matching AssetConfig.ledger_id.

editorial.description: Team-maintained asset information. Empty when never edited.

description.description: Plain text description, at most 10000 characters. Render as text.

discordUrl.description: Official HTTPS Discord URL, at most 2048 bytes.

explorerUrls.description: Up to 10 HTTPS block explorer URLs, each at most 2048 bytes; editorial order.

githubUrl.description: Official HTTPS GitHub URL, at most 2048 bytes.

issueDate.description: Launch calendar date as YYYY-MM-DD, or empty when unknown.

amount.description: Nonnegative decimal string, at most 64 characters; no exponent or sign.

telegramUrl.description: Official HTTPS Telegram URL, at most 2048 bytes.

websiteUrl.description: Official HTTPS website, at most 2048 bytes.

whitepaperUrl.description: HTTPS whitepaper URL, at most 2048 bytes.

xUrl.description: Official HTTPS X profile URL, at most 2048 bytes.

editorialUpdatedAt.description: Time of the last effective editorial change, in UTC. Absent when never edited.

marketStats.description: Market datapoints; absent when the asset has none.

circulatingSupply.description: Coins circulating in the market and in public hands, in asset units.

asOf.description: When the source last observed or set the value, in UTC. Older values stay until a newer observation replaces them, so show this time with the value.

value.description: Nonnegative decimal string without sign or exponent, at most 64 characters.

fullyDilutedMarketCapUsd.description: Price multiplied by maximum supply, or by total supply when the maximum is unknown or unlimited, in US dollars.

rank.description: Market capitalization rank among all listed coins as a positive integer string, where 1 is the largest.

code.description: Uppercase currency or stablecoin code, such as EUR or USDT.

fractionDigits.description: Default display fraction digits, including zero for currencies such as JPY. This is a formatting default, not rate precision, token decimals, or cash rounding. Stablecoins use two display fraction digits.

stablecoins.description: Supported stablecoins (USDC and USDT), ordered by code.

fiat.description: Complete fiat snapshot; absent until a complete snapshot has been observed.

rates.description: Complete fiat rates, including USD, ordered by code.

unitsPerUsd.description: Fiat currency units per 1 USD as an exact decimal string.

sourceTsSec.description: Shared source observation time in seconds since the Unix epoch (UTC).

snapshotTsSec.description: Response construction time in seconds since the Unix epoch (UTC).

stablecoins.description: Observed stablecoin rates ordered by code. Unobserved stablecoins are omitted.

code.description: Supported stablecoin code (USDC or USDT).

sourceTsSec.description: This stablecoin's source observation time in seconds since the Unix epoch (UTC).

stale.description: True once this stablecoin's source observation is at least five seconds old.

usdPerUnit.description: USD per 1 stablecoin unit as an exact decimal string.

bucket.description: Sampling interval between points; currently always "15m".

endTsSec.description: Last sample timestamp in seconds since Unix epoch (UTC), inclusive.

pairs.description: Pairs ordered by ascending symbol_id; at most 2000, each included once.

symbolId.description: Stable pair ID. Pairs are ordered by ascending ID, each included exactly once.

volumeUsd.description: Trailing-24h USD volume as decimal strings. Exactly points values aligned with the shared grid, oldest first. Zero means no executed trades.

points.description: Number of aligned values in every pair array and the total array; always 97.

startTsSec.description: First sample timestamp in seconds since Unix epoch (UTC), inclusive.

totalVolumeUsd.description: Total trailing-24h USD volume as decimal strings. Exactly points values, oldest first, aligned with every pair. Index i maps to startTsSec + i * 900 seconds. Zero means no trades; unavailable valuations fail the request.

markets.description: Market overview rows for the requested page.

bestAsk.description: Current best ask price as a decimal string in quote asset units.

bestAskQty.description: Best ask quantity as a decimal string in base asset units.

bestBid.description: Current best bid price as a decimal string in quote asset units.

bestBidQty.description: Best bid quantity as a decimal string in base asset units.

change24hBps.description: Rolling 24h change expressed in basis points (bp). Example: +123 = +1.23%. Measured from the 24h open to the last price, at minute granularity: the 24h open is the price at the start of the minute that contains the time 24h ago or, for a market that first traded later, its first trade. 0 while the 24h open is unavailable (open_24h_ticks is 0 then): the market has no trade yet (its last trade timestamp is 0 too), its first trade is a few seconds old, or its trade history is temporarily unavailable.

high24h.description: Highest price in the rolling 24h window, counting its open and every trade, as a decimal string in quote asset units.

indexPrice.description: Current multi-venue index price as a decimal string in quote asset units. Zero when no fresh, valid index price is available.

lastPrice.description: Last traded price as a decimal string in quote asset units, for example '28334.99'.

lastTradeTsNs.description: Last trade timestamp in nanoseconds since epoch.

listedTsNs.description: Listing timestamp in nanoseconds since epoch. 0 when the pair has no listing time.

low24h.description: Lowest price in the rolling 24h window, counting its open and every trade, as a decimal string in quote asset units.

open24h.description: The rolling 24h open that change24hBps is measured from, as a decimal string in quote asset units. Zero while the open is unavailable, including when history is temporarily unavailable: the market has no trade yet, its first trade is a few seconds old, or its trade history cannot be read for a while.

openUtcDay.description: Price at the start of the current UTC day (00:00 UTC), as a decimal string in quote asset units. Zero while the open is unavailable, including when history is temporarily unavailable: the market has no trade yet, a new day's first price is still being recorded (a few seconds after 00:00 UTC), or its trade history cannot be read for a while.

priceBand.description: The pair's live price band, as GetPriceBand returns it, present only while a band was confirmed current within the last 5 seconds. Absent means no fresh band is known, not that the pair has no band. This is a convenience copy: the market overview stream sends a row again when its band changes, appears or lapses, not on each confirmation, so a copy whose valid_until_ts_ns has passed is unknown. Check order prices against GetPriceBand or the price band stream.

asOf.description: When the band was last confirmed current.

epoch.description: The band's epoch, an unsigned 64-bit decimal string. It never decreases, and a band of a greater epoch is newer. Compare updateId only within one epoch.

maxBuyPrice.description: The highest buy limit price admitted, inclusive, as a decimal string. Present only when state is ACTIVE.

maxSellPrice.description: The highest sell limit price admitted, inclusive, as a decimal string. Present only when state is ACTIVE and the band limits passive prices too.

minBuyPrice.description: The lowest buy limit price admitted, inclusive, as a decimal string. Present only when state is ACTIVE and the band limits passive prices too.

minSellPrice.description: The lowest sell limit price admitted, inclusive, as a decimal string. Present only when state is ACTIVE.

parameters.description: The band's settings, as GetSpotConfig returns them. Absent when the state is OFF, or when the settings in effect cannot be expressed exactly in basis points and milliseconds; the limits above are authoritative either way.

lowerBps.description: How far below the reference price a sell may be priced or trade, in basis points (1 bp = 0.01%). The lower limit is the reference price times (1 - lower_bps / 10000), rounded up to the tick size.

referenceWindowMs.description: How long the reference price stays fixed before it can move to a newer trade, in milliseconds. Zero moves it with every order.

upperBps.description: How far above the reference price a buy may be priced or trade, in basis points. The upper limit is the reference price times (1 + upper_bps / 10000), rounded down to the tick size.

reanchorEligibleAt.description: From when the next order operation on the pair may move the reference price. Nothing moves at that time by itself. Present when state is ACTIVE or EMPTY.

reanchorPending.description: True when a trade newer than the reference price is waiting: once the re-anchor eligibility time has passed, the next order operation moves the reference to it, unless the index price moves it instead. False does not promise that the band stays: a move to the index price needs no trade.

referencePrice.description: The band's reference price as a decimal string in quote asset units per base asset unit, for example '61000.25'. Present when state is ACTIVE or EMPTY.

referenceSource.description: Where the reference price came from. REFERENCE_SOURCE_UNSPECIFIED when the state is OFF or UNKNOWN.

symbol.description: The pair's symbol, for example BTC-USDT.

updateId.description: Increases with each band update within an epoch, and may increase without one, as an unsigned 64-bit decimal string. Compare it only within one epoch: a greater value is newer.

updatedAt.description: When the band last changed: its first setting, OFF included, a change of its settings, or a move of its reference price, to the same price included.

validUntil.description: asOf plus 5 seconds. After it, treat the band as unknown and read it again.

close.description: Newest-first close prices as decimal strings in quote asset units.

interval.description: Time range and sampling resolution represented by these close prices.

stats1h.description: Rolling 1h stats, over the same minute-granular window as the 24h stats. Absent while the window's open is unavailable, including when history is temporarily unavailable: the market has no trade yet, its first trade is a few seconds old, or the window's trade history cannot be read for a while. Later fields may add volumes per window.

changeBps.description: Change from the open to the last price in basis points (bp), truncated toward zero. Example: +123 = +1.23%.

high.description: Highest price in the window, counting the open and every trade, as a decimal string in quote asset units.

low.description: Lowest price in the window, counting the open and every trade, as a decimal string in quote asset units.

open.description: Price at the start of the window as a decimal string in quote asset units: the last trade price before the window's first minute or, for a market that first traded later, its first trade.

stats4h.description: Rolling 4h stats. Absent under the same conditions as stats_1h.

tradeCount24h.description: Number of trades executed in the rolling 24h window, as an unsigned 64-bit decimal string.

volume24hBase.description: Rolling 24h base volume as a decimal string in base asset units. Omitted when the volume exceeds the supported range.

volume24hQuote.description: Rolling 24h executed quote volume as a decimal string in quote asset units. Omitted when the volume exceeds the supported range.

volume24hUsd.description: Rolling 24h USD volume as a decimal string in USD with up to 6 decimal places. Applies the current quote/USD conversion to the rolling quote volume. When conversion is unavailable, USDT and USDC are valued at USD parity. Omitted for other quote assets when a current conversion is unavailable.

vwap24h.description: Rolling 24h volume-weighted average trade price as a decimal string in quote asset units, rounded down: the exact quote notional divided by the 24h base volume. The notional is not rounded to the quote scale, so dividing volume24hQuote by volume24hBase can differ slightly. The base volume is exact when the base asset's marketDataVolumeScale equals its quantityScale; otherwise each second with trades rounds its base volume by at most half a volume unit. Omitted when the window has no base volume or volume24hBase is omitted.

nextPageToken.description: Opaque cursor for the next page. Empty when no more results exist.

asks.description: Best ask first; ascending price. When available is true, empty means no current liquidity; when it is false, always empty.

available.description: True when the book is current and empty sides mean no liquidity. False while the book is being built or after it was invalidated: its levels are unknown, not empty. Request the snapshot again later.

bids.description: Best bid first; descending price. When available is true, empty means no current liquidity; when it is false, always empty.

bookEpoch.description: Epoch of bookSeq, as a decimal string. Order snapshots by (bookEpoch, bookSeq): a higher epoch is newer whatever its bookSeq, and a new epoch may restart bookSeq. Discard a snapshot whose epoch is older than the newest one seen for the symbol. 0 while available is false.

bookSeq.description: Book sequence of this snapshot within bookEpoch, as a decimal string. Monotonic within one epoch; compare it only with sequences of the same epoch.

depth.description: Depth tier this snapshot was served at: the depth query parameter, or 50 when it was omitted. Set in every response, available or not.

ts.description: Snapshot timestamp as Unix epoch milliseconds; 0 while available is false.

nextPageToken.description: Opaque cursor for the next page. Empty when no more results exist.

attachedRisk.description: Attached risk controls + runtime state on the parent order. Empty when no attached risk exists. Order reads include it only when the request asks for it (include_attached_risk, include_attached_risk_state): an omission on request, never a removal. The private WebSocket always carries it in full, as a read asking for both does.

oco.description: True while the parent's legs were placed with oco and both the take-profit and a stop leg (stop-loss or trailing stop) are present. False once either leg is removed. A leg that ended, including one canceled with OCO, stays present.

stopLoss.description: Stop-loss leg, if configured or if state exists.

policy.description: Stop-loss policy configured on the parent order.

child.description: Required child execution when the threshold is crossed.

price.description: Limit price as a decimal string in quote asset units per base asset unit, for example '61000.25'.

marketIoc.description: Market child with implicit IOC behavior.

triggerPrice.description: Trigger price as a decimal string in quote asset units per base asset unit, for example '60000'.

triggerPriceSource.description: Price the stop-loss watches. Unspecified or LAST_PRICE watches the last traded price. INDEX_PRICE watches the market's index price; on a market without an index price the order is rejected before any fill with reject_reason TRIGGER_PRICE_SOURCE_UNSUPPORTED, and a modify that adds such a leg is refused with the same code, leaving the order and its legs unchanged. childOrderId.description: Child order ID created by this leg after it fires.

terminalAt.description: Time the leg reached a terminal state, in nanoseconds since epoch (UTC). Zero if not terminal.

takeProfit.description: Take-profit leg, if configured or if state exists.

armedAt.description: Time the leg was armed, in nanoseconds since epoch (UTC). Zero if not armed.

terminalAt.description: Time the leg reached a terminal state, in nanoseconds since epoch (UTC). Zero if not terminal.

trailingStop.description: Trailing-stop leg, if configured or if state exists.

activationPrice.description: Optional activation price as a decimal string in quote asset units per base asset unit, for example '62000': trailing only starts after this price is reached. If omitted, trailing starts immediately after the parent order fills.

limitPrice.description: Maximum price of a trailing stop that buys back, as a decimal string in quote asset units per base asset unit, for example '65000': the most its exit pays, at which the quote it may spend is reserved. Present when the parent order sells; omitted when the parent order buys.

maxSlippageBps.description: Maximum allowed slippage in basis points (1 bp = 0.01%), from 1 to 9999 whichever side the exit trades. An order whose trailing stop sets 10000 is rejected with MAX_SLIPPAGE_INVALID, because a 100% cap would leave an exit that sells no positive price to sell at.

maxSlippageTicks.description: Maximum absolute price delta of the exit's protection price from the price that fired it, as a positive integer in 1e-9 quote units, for example 50120000000 for 50.12. The ticks in this name are 1e-9 quote units, not the pair's price tick, and the value need not be a multiple of the pair's tick: the protection price is rounded onto the tick grid toward the firing price, a buy's down and a sell's up.

trailingDistance.description: Trailing distance as a decimal price delta in quote asset units, for example '0.5'.

trailingDistanceBps.description: Trailing distance in basis points (1 bp = 0.01%), from 1 to 10000.

triggerPriceSource.description: Price the trailing stop watches and trails: its peak or trough, activation and fire all follow this price. Unspecified or LAST_PRICE watches the last traded price. policy.description: Trailing-stop policy configured on the parent order.

activationPrice.description: Optional activation price as a decimal string in quote asset units per base asset unit, for example '62000': trailing only starts after this price is reached. If omitted, trailing starts immediately after the parent order fills.

limitPrice.description: Maximum price of a trailing stop that buys back, as a decimal string in quote asset units per base asset unit, for example '65000': the most its exit pays, at which the quote it may spend is reserved. Present when the parent order sells; omitted when the parent order buys.

maxSlippageBps.description: Maximum allowed slippage in basis points (1 bp = 0.01%), from 1 to 9999 whichever side the exit trades. An order whose trailing stop sets 10000 is rejected with MAX_SLIPPAGE_INVALID, because a 100% cap would leave an exit that sells no positive price to sell at.

maxSlippageTicks.description: Maximum absolute price delta of the exit's protection price from the price that fired it, as a positive integer in 1e-9 quote units, for example 50120000000 for 50.12. The ticks in this name are 1e-9 quote units, not the pair's price tick, and the value need not be a multiple of the pair's tick: the protection price is rounded onto the tick grid toward the firing price, a buy's down and a sell's up.

trailingDistance.description: Trailing distance as a decimal price delta in quote asset units, for example '0.5'.

trailingDistanceBps.description: Trailing distance in basis points (1 bp = 0.01%), from 1 to 10000.

triggerPriceSource.description: Price the trailing stop watches and trails: its peak or trough, activation and fire all follow this price. Unspecified or LAST_PRICE watches the last traded price. INDEX_PRICE watches the market's index price; on a market without an index price the order is rejected before any fill with reject_reason TRIGGER_PRICE_SOURCE_UNSUPPORTED, and a modify that adds such a leg is refused with the same code, leaving the order and its legs unchanged. MARK_PRICE is not supported. A modify naming another source replaces the leg.

state.description: Runtime state for the trailing-stop leg.

armedAt.description: Time the leg was armed, in nanoseconds since epoch (UTC). Zero if not armed.

childOrderId.description: Child order ID created by this leg after it fires.

status.description: Current runtime lifecycle status for this attached-risk leg.

terminalAt.description: Time the leg reached a terminal state, in nanoseconds since epoch (UTC). Zero if not terminal.

triggerId.description: Trigger identifier for this attached-risk leg.

avgPx.description: Average execution price across the lineage through this generation, as a decimal string in quote asset units per base asset unit, for example '0.000002908714285714': the exact executed quote amount divided by cumQty, rounded half to even at 18 decimal places, trailing zeros trimmed. '0' if no fills.

batchRequestId.description: Batch-replace identity that admitted this order, retained after it ends. Also set for batch-replaced trigger-generated orders. Zero when this order was not admitted by a batch replacement; a later batch replacing this order does not change its admission identity.

cancelReason.description: For a CANCELED order, why it ended. Not set for every other status; JSON and REST responses then omit it.

clientOrderId.description: Client-provided, account-scoped identifier for correlation, lookup, and cancellation. Empty when none was supplied.

createdAt.description: Creation timestamp in nanoseconds since epoch (UTC).

cumQty.description: Cumulative filled quantity across the lineage through this generation, as a decimal string in base asset units, for example '0.0005'.

cumQuote.description: Exact quote amount of the fills across the lineage through this generation, before fees, as a decimal string in quote asset units, for example '3215.5809531728'. For a BUY sized by submittedMaxQuoteDebit, the quote it used is cumQuote plus feeTotal.amount when feeAsset is QUOTE, or minus it when feeTotal.isRebate is true, since a rebate is credited, and cumQuote alone when feeAsset is BASE; submittedMaxQuoteDebit less the quote it used is what it left unspent. For a SELL sized by submittedQuoteProceeds, cumQuote is the proceeds it received before fees, never above it; it was credited cumQuote less feeTotal.amount, or plus it when feeTotal.isRebate is true, and submittedQuoteProceeds less cumQuote is what it did not receive. '0' if no fills. Each fill settles its quote rounded down to 18 decimal places, so cumQuote is exactly the quote the fills settled when the base asset's quantity scale is at most 9; above that, cumQuote can exceed it by less than 1e-18 per fill.

displayQty.description: Iceberg display quantity the order was placed with, as a decimal string in base asset units, for example '0.01': the most of the order the order book shows at once. '0' for a plain order. A replace keeps it.

expireAt.description: Exact UTC expiry time for GTD orders, within the supported signed Unix-nanosecond range from 1677-09-21T00:12:43.145224193Z through 2262-04-11T23:47:16.854775807Z. Omitted for all other time-in-force policies. The order cannot execute when the current time equals this value.

feeAsset.description: Fee asset selected for fills. Unset for the replacement order of a batch item refused when it applied (REJECTED with batch_request_id set), which never existed and carries no order terms: the client knows them from the batch it sent.

feeTotal.description: Total fee of the fills across the lineage through this generation, net of rebates, in the order's fee asset. A fill's fee is recorded once the fill is settled, which can be seconds after the order ended. Order history reads and single-order reads that include execution history (the default) carry it, over the fills recorded so far: its quantity shows which fills it covers, and it is the order's whole fee once that quantity equals the order's filled quantity. Open-order reads, single-order reads without execution history and private stream order updates leave it unset, an ended order's update included. To show the fee of an order seen on the private stream, or the quote a BUY sized by a quote amount used: once an update shows the order ended with a filled quantity above zero, read the order by its ID, and read it again, a few hundred milliseconds apart, until the fee total's quantity equals the order's filled quantity.

amount.description: Net fee of the fills the total covers, their fees less their rebates, as a decimal string in feeAsset units, for example '0.96467428595184'. '0' when they charged no fee.

isRebate.description: True when the covered fills' rebates exceed their fees, so the amount was credited to the account rather than charged.

qty.description: Executed quantity of the fills the total covers, as a decimal string in base asset units, for example '0.04148504'. Equal to the order's cumQty once every fill's fee is recorded; while a fill is still being recorded the two differ, and a later read includes it.

hiddenQty.description: Part of leavesQty an iceberg order keeps hidden from the order book, as a decimal string in base asset units, for example '0.04'. The order book shows leavesQty minus this quantity. '0' for a plain order and for terminal orders.

inheritedCumQty.description: Cumulative filled base quantity inherited from predecessors when this replacement was accepted, as a decimal string in base asset units, for example '0.0005'. '0' for the original order and immutable within a generation. cumQty minus this value is the quantity executed by this generation, not the quantity new to a client session.

leavesQty.description: Remaining working quantity as a decimal string in base asset units, for example '0.001'. '0' for terminal orders.

lineage.description: Logical-order identity and requested generation. Always populated by order reads. A batch item's refused replacement never joined its predecessor's lineage: it is its own, at generation 1.

generation.description: One-based replacement generation, distinct from per-order state version.

id.description: Stable logical-order ID: the first generation's public order ID. Replace preserves this ID; an independent new order starts a new lineage.

marketClientRefPrice.description: Client reference price the MARKET order set for its slippage protection, as a decimal string in quote asset units per base asset unit, for example '73840.125', exactly as given: it need not be a multiple of the pair's price tick. '0' when the order set none.

marketMaxSlippageBps.description: Optional MARKET max slippage in basis points (1 bp = 0.01%).

marketMaxSlippageTicks.description: Maximum absolute price delta the MARKET order set, as an integer in 1e-9 quote units (not the pair's price tick), exactly as given: it need not be a multiple of the pair's tick. 0 when the order set none, for example because it set marketMaxSlippageBps instead.

orderType.description: Order type. Unset for the replacement order of a batch item refused when it applied (REJECTED with batch_request_id set), which never existed and carries no order terms: the client knows them from the batch it sent.

origQty.description: Current accepted total order quantity, updated by successful modifies, as a decimal string in base asset units, for example '0.001'.

origin.description: Runtime lineage metadata (why the order exists and what generated it).

childSeq.description: Child sequence number for multi-child trigger strategies. Zero when not applicable.

parentOrderId.description: Parent order ID for attached-risk child orders.

scope.description: Broad class describing how the order was created.

triggerId.description: Trigger identifier when the order was created by a trigger.

triggerType.description: Trigger strategy that created this order. Not set for direct orders; JSON and REST responses then omit it.

postOnly.description: True if the order was submitted as post-only (maker-only).

price.description: Price as a decimal string in quote asset units per base asset unit, for example '61000.25'. For a LIMIT order, its limit price. For a MARKET order, whatever placed it, its protection price: the worst price it may fill at, a BUY at or below it and a SELL at or above it. It is the order's reference price moved by its maximum slippage, or by the pair's default market slippage for its side (200 basis points if none is configured), rounded onto the pair's tick grid toward the reference (a BUY's down, a SELL's up), so it never allows more than the slippage; the reference and the slippage need not be on the tick grid themselves. A stop-loss's, take-profit's or trailing stop's market order takes the price that fired it as its reference; a buy stop's is never above the protection price at its trigger price.

rejectReason.description: For a REJECTED order, why it was refused: the same error code the Orders API returns for the same refusal. Not set for every other status; JSON and REST responses then omit it.

side.description: Order side. Unset for the replacement order of a batch item refused when it applied (REJECTED with batch_request_id set), which never existed and carries no order terms: the client knows them from the batch it sent.

stpMode.description: Self-trade prevention mode. Unset for the replacement order of a batch item refused when it applied (REJECTED with batch_request_id set), which never existed and carries no order terms: the client knows them from the batch it sent.

submittedMaxQuoteDebit.description: Submitted hard all-in quote debit limit as a decimal string in quote asset units, for example '100'. Present only when that sizing method was submitted.

submittedQuoteProceeds.description: Submitted quote proceeds target as a decimal string in quote asset units, for example '100'. Present only when that sizing method was submitted.

symbol.description: Trading symbol numeric identifier. Unset for the replacement order of a batch item refused when it applied (REJECTED with batch_request_id set), which never existed and carries no order terms: the client knows them from the batch it sent.

terminalAt.description: Terminal timestamp in nanoseconds since epoch (UTC). Zero for open orders.

tif.description: Time-in-force policy. Unset for the replacement order of a batch item refused when it applied (REJECTED with batch_request_id set), which never existed and carries no order terms: the client knows them from the batch it sent.

version.description: Per-order state version: the same counter as the version of the order's events on the private WebSocket and the trade WebSocket. It is 0 while the order is accepted but not yet on the book (status PENDING), then 1 from its first book state, and it increases with every later published change of the order's state, such as an amend in place, a fill, a change of its attached risk, a cancel or a replace. It is an unsigned 32-bit counter that increases on every change of the order: it would wrap to 0 only after 4,294,967,295 changes to one order ID. A replace that gives the order a new ID starts that order's own version. A read can lag behind the order's events. Keep the highest version applied for each order ID, from reads and events alike, and drop any read whose version is below it: that read shows an older state. A stream need not show every version, so a gap is not an error; read the order to recover its current state. fee_total is not covered by this version: a fill's fee is recorded after the fill, so responses with the same version can show different fee totals. A read includes attached_risk only on request, so its absence from a response is no change of the order.

nextPageToken.description: Opaque cursor for the next page. Empty when no more results exist.

trades.description: Trades ordered by timestamp, symbol, match and physical order, descending. Projection is eventual: an empty page is not proof of order-state reconciliation.

executedAt.description: Execution timestamp in nanoseconds since epoch.

fee.description: Exact fee magnitude as a decimal string in feeAsset units, for example '0.0305'.

feeAsset.description: Fee asset charged or credited for this fill.

feeIsRebate.description: Whether this fill earned a rebate instead of paying a fee.

isMaker.description: True if this fill was maker-side.

lineage.description: Logical-order identity and the generation that executed this fill. Always populated by execution reads; order_id retains its original identity.

generation.description: One-based replacement generation, distinct from per-order state version.

id.description: Stable logical-order ID: the first generation's public order ID. Replace preserves this ID; an independent new order starts a new lineage.

orderId.description: Public order ID of the filled order.

price.description: Execution price as a decimal string in quote asset units per base asset unit, for example '61000.25'.

qty.description: Executed quantity as a decimal string in base asset units, for example '0.001'.

referralShare.description: Exact referral share magnitude as a decimal string in feeAsset units, for example '0.0061'.

side.description: Fill side.

transfers.description: Settlement legs for matches represented on this page, when requested.

account.description: Account bucket affected by this transfer leg.

asset.description: Asset identifier for the transferred asset.

isDebit.description: True when the transfer debits the account; false when it credits the account.

matchId.description: Match identifier that linked this transfer to an execution, scoped by symbol_id.

symbolId.description: Market of the execution; together with match_id identifies its match.

timestamp.description: Transfer timestamp in nanoseconds since epoch (UTC).

transferCode.description: Product reason for this transfer leg.

polyester.rest.OrdersService.Problem.description: Order request error. OVERLOADED returns HTTP 503 when the account has too many order requests in flight; nothing was admitted. No Retry-After or RateLimit-* headers are supplied; retry after an outstanding request completes. Quota exhaustion returns HTTP 429 with RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED and rate-limit metadata.

code.description: Stable order error code.

detail.description: Human-readable explanation; clients must branch on code.

existingOrderId.description: Public order ID holding this account's client order ID on CONFLICT_DUPLICATE_CLIENT_ORDER_ID; omitted when no existing holder is known. Use GetOrder for current state.

rateLimit.description: RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED (HTTP 429) and RATE_LIMIT_AUTHORITY_UNAVAILABLE (HTTP 503) only: the rate-limit decision, with the fields of a batch item error's rateLimit; limit, remaining, retryAfterMs and policyVersion are decimal strings here. A 429 the API gateway answers before the request reaches the service carries only reason (QUOTA_EXCEEDED) and scope (CLIENT_IP). Omitted for every other code.

limit.description: Active weighted quota. Present for the service's RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED.

operationId.description: Stable operation identifier shared by all aliases of the same action. Present when the service refused the request; absent on the API gateway's own 429.

policyClass.description: Mutable quota family used for the decision. Present when the service refused the request; absent on the API gateway's own 429.

policyVersion.description: Policy version used for the decision, when available.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure reason.

refillModel.description: Refill behavior used by the active limiter. Present when the service refused the request; absent on the API gateway's own 429.

remaining.description: Weighted capacity remaining when the request was rejected. Present for the service's RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED.

retryAfterMs.description: Minimum relative delay before retrying, in milliseconds. Present for the service's RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED; on the API gateway's own 429, use the Retry-After header.

scope.description: Caller dimension that owns the exhausted capacity.

timestampWindow.description: TIMESTAMP_SKEW only: the server time and the window the request's X-API-TIMESTAMP had to fall in, from serverTimeMs minus recvWindowMs to serverTimeMs plus maxFutureMs, both inclusive. Omitted for every other code.

maxFutureMs.description: How far a timestamp may run ahead of the server time, in milliseconds: 1000.

recvWindowMs.description: Receive window the timestamp was checked against, in milliseconds: the request's X-API-RECV-WINDOW, or 5000 when the header is omitted.

serverTimeMs.description: Server time when the request was refused, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch, as a decimal string.

type.description: URI identifying the problem type: https://polyester.dev/problems/ followed by code in lowercase, with hyphens for underscores, for example https://polyester.dev/problems/rate-limit-exceeded for RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED.

violations.description: Field-level validation failures, the violations ConnectRPC returns for the same request, each naming the REST request field; omitted when there are none.

fieldPath.description: REST path of the request field the violation names, for example order.baseQty or items[2].limitGtc.price; when no choice of a one-of group was sent, the group, for example order.execution.

ruleId.description: Stable validation rule identifier suitable for programmatic matching.

clientOrderId.description: Client order ID: 1 to 36 ASCII characters using letters, digits, period, underscore, colon, slash, or hyphen. Exactly one of order_id or client_order_id.

orderId.description: Public order ID. Exactly one of order_id or client_order_id.

requestId.description: Idempotency key (required). 1 to 64 ASCII characters using letters, digits, period, underscore, colon, slash, or hyphen.

subaccountId.description: Optional public subaccount ID. When omitted, subaccount-scoped API keys use their bound subaccount; other callers use their authenticated root account.

acceptedCount.description: Number of requested cancellations that were accepted.

rejectedCount.description: Number of requested cancellations that were rejected.

results.description: Per-item results in same order as request.

code.description: Error code if rejected.

error.description: Structured rejection details. Present for rate-limit guidance and other typed failures.

policyVersion.description: Policy version used for the decision, when available.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure reason.

refillModel.description: Refill behavior used by the active limiter.

retryAfterMs.description: Minimum relative delay before retrying, in milliseconds.

tsNs.description: Server timestamp as epoch nanoseconds (for bots).

items.description: Orders to create, 1 to 20. client_order_id is optional per item. For a new request_id, a reused client_order_id rejects only that item with CONFLICT_DUPLICATE_CLIENT_ORDER_ID; other valid items continue.

attachedRisk.description: Optional attached risk controls that arm after the parent order fills.

oco.description: If true, the take-profit and the configured stop leg (stop-loss or trailing stop) are linked and shown as one-cancels-the-other. Requires a take-profit and exactly one stop leg. The legs of every parent share one position and end together as described on RiskPolicy, so this setting does not change when exits are submitted. It decides only what canceling a leg's exit order ends: with oco set, canceling one leg's exit ends both legs; without it, only that leg ends and the other keeps protecting the remaining position. Canceling a leg itself with CancelTrigger ends only that leg either way, and the other leg stays active. Changing only this setting with ModifyOrder keeps the existing legs, with their IDs, arming and a trailing stop's tracked peak; changing a leg's terms, such as its trigger price, limit price or trailing distance, still replaces that leg. Default is false.

child.description: Required child execution when the threshold is crossed.

price.description: Limit price as a decimal string in quote asset units per base asset unit, for example '61000.25'.

marketIoc.description: Market child with implicit IOC behavior.

MARK_PRICE is not supported. A modify naming another source replaces the leg.

baseQty.description: Exact gross base quantity as a human-readable decimal using the pair's base quantity scale.

clientOrderId.description: Optional account-scoped identifier for correlation, lookup, and cancellation. While this identifier is retained, reuse returns CONFLICT_DUPLICATE_CLIENT_ORDER_ID for every new submission, even with the same payload. This identifier enables GetOrder reconciliation after a timeout; it does not provide exact replay. At most 36 ASCII characters using letters, digits, period, underscore, colon, slash, or hyphen.

feeAsset.description: Asset charged for fees. Defaults to QUOTE. BASE is available only for BUY orders on a pair whose allow_buy_fee_from_base is true in GetSpotConfig; SELL orders must use QUOTE. Otherwise the order is refused with FEE_ASSET_NOT_ALLOWED.

price.description: Limit price as a decimal string in quote asset units per base asset unit, for example '61000.25'.

limitGtc.description: Resting GTC limit order, optionally post-only.

displayQty.description: Optional iceberg display quantity as a decimal string in base asset units, for example '0.01'. Omit it for a plain order. The order book shows at most this quantity of the order; once that shown part is fully executed, the next part is shown at the same price, behind the orders already resting there. It must be below baseQty, a multiple of the pair's quantity step, at least the pair's minimum quantity, and at least baseQty divided by 100, rounded up, so the order splits into at most 100 parts. An iceberg order cannot carry attachedRisk. The display cannot be modified; a replace keeps it.

postOnly.description: Reject the order instead of taking liquidity. Post-only is available only on this resting limit-order variant. Defaults to false when omitted.

price.description: Limit price as a decimal string in quote asset units per base asset unit, for example '61000.25'.

limitGtd.description: Limit order with an exact expiry time.

displayQty.description: Optional iceberg display quantity as a decimal string in base asset units, for example '0.01'. Omit it for a plain order. The order book shows at most this quantity of the order; once that shown part is fully executed, the next part is shown at the same price, behind the orders already resting there. It must be below baseQty, a multiple of the pair's quantity step, at least the pair's minimum quantity, and at least baseQty divided by 100, rounded up, so the order splits into at most 100 parts. An iceberg order cannot carry attachedRisk. The display cannot be modified; a replace keeps it.

expireAt.description: Required exact expiry time in UTC. It must be at least 1 second and at most 30 days after validation time. The order cannot execute when the current time equals this value.

Limit price as a decimal string in quote asset units per base asset unit, for example '61000.25'.

marketIoc.description: Market order with implicit IOC behavior.

clientRefPrice.description: Optional client reference price for the market order's slippage protection, as a decimal string in quote asset units per base asset unit, for example '61000.25'. It need not be a multiple of the pair's price tick: only the protection price derived from it is. The protection price is the reference moved by the maximum slippage, up for a BUY and down for a SELL, then rounded onto the pair's tick grid toward the reference (a BUY's down, a SELL's up), so it never allows more than the slippage and can be up to one tick tighter. For example, with a 0.01 tick, a reference of '73840.125' and a maximum slippage of 50.12 quote units give a BUY protection price of 73890.24 and a SELL protection price of 73790.01. When omitted, admission uses server-side reference pricing. A reference too far from the server's is refused with STALE_QUOTE.

maxSlippageBps.description: Maximum allowed slippage in basis points (1 bp = 0.01%), from 1 to 10000. A SELL order accepts at most 9999: a 100% cap would leave it no positive price to sell at, so 10000 is rejected with MAX_SLIPPAGE_INVALID.

maxSlippageTicks.description: Maximum absolute price delta of the protection price from the reference price, as a positive integer in 1e-9 quote units, for example 50120000000 for 50.12. The ticks in this name are 1e-9 quote units, not the pair's price tick, and the value need not be a multiple of the pair's tick: the protection price is rounded onto the tick grid toward the reference, as clientRefPrice describes.

maxQuoteDebit.description: Hard all-in quote debit limit as a decimal string in quote asset units, for example '100'. Valid only for BUY market IOC and BUY limit IOC.

peg.description: Optional static peg. The selected limit execution still requires its price bound. Quote sizing, market execution and attached risk are invalid.

offsetTicks.description: Signed number of configured price increments added once at entry. The limit price is the required buy cap or sell floor.

reference.description: Required public book side. An empty selected side rejects the order.

quoteProceeds.description: Quote proceeds target before fees as a decimal string in quote asset units, for example '100'. The order sells whole quantity steps until its proceeds reach this amount, never more. Valid only for SELL market IOC and SELL limit IOC.

selfTradePreventionMode.description: Self-trade prevention mode against orders of the same root account, including all its subaccounts. Defaults to EXPIRE_MAKER if unspecified.

side.description: Order side. Required.

requestId.description: Required account-scoped idempotency key for the entire ordered batch. Reusing it with the same payload within 15 minutes returns each decided item's original result and result time, and retries the items still unresolved, never admitting an already admitted item again. Reusing it with a different payload during that window returns CONFLICT_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSE. After 15 minutes the ID is free: a repeat is a new request and can place its orders again, so read the items back instead of repeating an older batch. 1 to 64 ASCII characters using letters, digits, period, underscore, colon, slash, or hyphen.

subaccountId.description: Optional public subaccount ID. When omitted, subaccount-scoped API keys use their bound subaccount; other callers use their authenticated root account.

acceptedCount.description: Number of requested orders that were accepted.

rejectedCount.description: Number of requested orders that were rejected.

results.description: Per-item results in same order as request.

resolvedBaseQtyScaled.description: Gross base quantity admission resolved, as a scaled integer. For baseQty sizing, the order's quantity. For quote sizing (maxQuoteDebit BUY or quoteProceeds SELL), the quantity the quote amount buys or sells at the order's limit price, or a market order's protection price: a BUY can fill more at better prices, or less when the book runs out, and a SELL sells at most this. The executed quantity is the order's cumulative filled quantity (cumQty in GetOrder) or the sum of its fills (GetUserTrades, or the fills of its private order events). Batch results preserve the canonical scaled value because one batch can contain multiple symbols; use the corresponding request item's symbol base quantity scale to decode it.

stopLossTriggerId.description: Trigger ID for attached stop-loss (when accepted and configured).

submittedMaxQuoteDebitScaled.description: Submitted hard all-in quote debit limit, scaled by the pair's quote_quantity_scale from GetSpotConfig. Present only when submitted.

submittedQuoteProceedsScaled.description: Submitted quote proceeds target, scaled by the pair's quote_quantity_scale from GetSpotConfig. Present only when submitted.

takeProfitTriggerId.description: Trigger ID for attached take-profit (when accepted and configured).

trailingStopTriggerId.description: Trigger ID for attached trailing stop (when accepted and configured).

error.description: Structured rejection detail. Its violations name the item's fields as a CreateOrderRequest carrying the item would, under order (for example order.limit_gtc.price_ticks), not under items; the item is this result's position in the response. REST names them as a REST create carrying the item would (for example order.limitGtc.price).

items.description: Replacement items, 1 to 50, each targeting a different order.

newAttachedRisk.description: Replacement attached-risk policy for the order.

oco.description: If true, the take-profit and the configured stop leg (stop-loss or trailing stop) are linked and shown as one-cancels-the-other. Requires a take-profit and exactly one stop leg. The legs of every parent share one position and end together as described on RiskPolicy, so this setting does not change when exits are submitted. It decides only what canceling a leg's exit order ends: with oco set, canceling one leg's exit ends both legs; without it, only that leg ends and the other keeps protecting the remaining position. Canceling a leg itself with CancelTrigger ends only that leg either way, and the other leg stays active. Changing only this setting with ModifyOrder keeps the existing legs, with their IDs, arming and a trailing stop's tracked peak; changing a leg's terms, such as its trigger price, limit price or trailing distance, still replaces that leg. Default is false.

triggerPriceSource.description: Price the stop-loss watches. Unspecified or LAST_PRICE watches the last traded price. MARK_PRICE is not supported. A modify naming another source replaces the leg.

includeTriggers.description: If true, the switch's expiry also stops the account's triggers in its scope, as CancelAllOrders with `include_triggers` does: those created before the expiry time, even when the expiry is processed later, and none of them places an order once it is processed. A trigger created at or after the expiry time is not stopped. Defaults to false: only orders are canceled on expiry. Each arm or refresh sets it again; a disable ignores it.

effectiveScope.description: Recorded scope after arming or refreshing. Absent when disabled. Describes the current armed switch only. Cancellations already in progress are unaffected by a later refresh or disable.

dryRun.description: If true, return matched counts without actually canceling.

includeTriggers.description: If true, also stops the account's triggers in the same scope: every stop-loss, take-profit, trailing stop, TWAP, ladder, standalone OCO (both its legs) and attached take-profit, stop-loss or trailing leg on the matched symbols whose orders trade on the side filter, created before the request was accepted. Each ends canceled with reason `CANCEL_ALL` and releases its reserved funds, its open orders are canceled with the others, and none places an order after the response. Defaults to false: only orders are canceled and triggers keep running. Part of the criteria a retry must keep.

requestId.description: Idempotency key (required). Reuse the same key and criteria for retries. Completed results are retained for at least two minutes. Use a fresh key for a new cancellation; do not reuse a key after its replay window. 1 to 64 ASCII characters using letters, digits, period, underscore, colon, slash, or hyphen.

side.description: Side filter. When set, only orders on this side are canceled.

subaccountId.description: Optional public subaccount ID. When omitted, subaccount-scoped API keys use their bound subaccount; other callers use their authenticated root account.

symbols.description: Up to 100 trading pair symbols, e.g. [BTC-USDT, ETH-USDT]. Empty matches all symbols; duplicates are ignored.

cancelledOrders.description: Orders whose cancellation was requested, oldest first (the order in which they were created), at most 200. When more orders were canceled, these are the 200 oldest and `truncated` is true; the order update stream and read paths report every one. Empty when `dry_run` is set. Retrying with the same `request_id` and criteria within 120 seconds returns the original status, counts and timestamp, an empty list, and `listing_status = NOT_RETAINED_READ_OPEN_ORDERS`. It requests no new cancellations. Read open orders for current state and use order updates for final outcomes.

clientOrderId.description: The order's client order ID; empty when the order has none.

failedCancels.description: Number of matched orders that could not be submitted for cancellation because the cancel-all could not be recorded for their symbol. This request does not cancel them; send a new cancel-all with a new `request_id` if they are still open. Zero when `dry_run` is set.

listingStatus.description: Availability of the historical listing. An empty retry listing does not change the original counts or mean that no cancellations were requested.

matchedOrders.description: Number of open orders that matched the filter when the request was accepted, including orders whose cancellation was already in progress and open orders that triggers placed. Triggers themselves are never counted. Orders placed after acceptance are not counted. Unless `dry_run` is set, equals `submitted_cancels` plus `failed_cancels`.

matchedTriggers.description: With `include_triggers`, the number of the account's triggers that matched the filters when the request was accepted, each stopped unless `dry_run` is set. Zero without `include_triggers`.

submittedCancels.description: Number of matched orders for which cancellation was requested, including orders whose cancellation was already in progress. Observe order updates or reads for final outcomes; orders may execute before cancellation takes effect. Zero when `dry_run` is set.

totalCancelled.description: Number of orders whose cancellation was requested, including those not listed in `cancelled_orders`. Equals `submitted_cancels`. Zero when `dry_run` is set.

truncated.description: True when more orders were canceled than `cancelled_orders` lists.

price.description: Limit price as a decimal string in quote asset units per base asset unit, for example '61000.25'.

limitGtc.description: Resting GTC limit order, optionally post-only.

displayQty.description: Optional iceberg display quantity as a decimal string in base asset units, for example '0.01'. Omit it for a plain order. The order book shows at most this quantity of the order; once that shown part is fully executed, the next part is shown at the same price, behind the orders already resting there. It must be below baseQty, a multiple of the pair's quantity step, at least the pair's minimum quantity, and at least baseQty divided by 100, rounded up, so the order splits into at most 100 parts. An iceberg order cannot carry attachedRisk. The display cannot be modified; a replace keeps it.

postOnly.description: Reject the order instead of taking liquidity. Post-only is available only on this resting limit-order variant. Defaults to false when omitted.
