x-poly-enum-descriptions.TRIGGER_WOULD_TRIGGER_IMMEDIATELY: The trigger price, or a trailing stop's activation price, was already reached by the price the trigger watches (at or past it) when the trigger took effect, a few milliseconds after it was submitted, so the trigger would have fired or activated at once. It never armed and sent no order; its reserved funds were released. A price that reaches it after the trigger is armed, or for a trailing stop created, fires or activates the trigger normally.
x-poly-enum-descriptions.TWAP_CAPACITY_REACHED: The market had no room for another TWAP order.
x-poly-enum-descriptions.TWAP_INTERVAL_INVALID: The TWAP interval was not valid.
x-poly-enum-descriptions.UNKNOWN_SYMBOL: The requested trading pair was not recognized.
x-poly-enum-descriptions.UNSUPPORTED_FIELD_SET: The trigger set a field that must be left unset.

x-poly-enum-descriptions.ARMED: Trigger admitted and actively evaluating conditions.
x-poly-enum-descriptions.CANCELED: Trigger was canceled. The cancel reason states why, for example a user request or another attached leg's exit closing its parent's position. A ladder is canceled when the ladder itself is canceled. A ladder whose child orders the user canceled with none filled, one by one, with a cancel-all or by the dead man's switch, is canceled too, with a user request reason, once none of them remains open. A ladder whose child orders were canceled only by self-trade prevention, or by the exchange while it recovered the account, with none filled, completes instead.
x-poly-enum-descriptions.COMPLETED: Trigger completed. A ladder completes once none of its child orders remains open and at least one of them was placed on the book, unless it ends canceled (see CANCELED). A ladder that filled any quantity completes however its other child orders ended. Some of its child orders may have been rejected. Completed does not mean the ladder filled: its executed quantity and executed levels state what filled, and each child order's own status states how it ended.
x-poly-enum-descriptions.CREATED: Trigger was created and is pending activation.
x-poly-enum-descriptions.FAILED: Trigger failed (for example, reservation failure, child order rejection). A ladder fails when every child order was rejected before it was placed on the book; the failure reason is the first rejected child order's.
x-poly-enum-descriptions.PAUSED: Trigger is paused (user-initiated, can be resumed).
x-poly-enum-descriptions.RUNNING: Trigger is actively executing (for example, TWAP slices in progress).

x-poly-enum-descriptions.LADDER: Ladder/Scaled: Multiple orders placed across a price range.
x-poly-enum-descriptions.STOP_LOSS: Stop-loss: a SELL fires when the price falls to or below its trigger price, a BUY when the price rises to or above it.
x-poly-enum-descriptions.TAKE_PROFIT: Take-profit: a SELL fires when the price rises to or above its trigger price, a BUY when the price falls to or below it.
x-poly-enum-descriptions.TRAILING_STOP: Trailing stop: dynamic stop that trails price by a distance.
x-poly-enum-descriptions.TWAP: TWAP: Time-Weighted Average Price execution over a duration.

post.description: Cancel all matching open orders for an account. Supports an optional list of symbols and a side filter plus dry-run preview. Returns up to 200 canceled order IDs, oldest first, with the total count. Unless it is a dry run, it covers every matching order admitted before its requestId was first admitted, from any interface, including orders not yet open and replacement orders: an order whose create or replace response arrived before the first request with this requestId was sent is covered, while requests still in flight or with an unknown outcome have no defined order with it. A retry with the same requestId keeps the original scope and covers no order admitted since; use a fresh requestId for a new cancellation. Each covered order eventually ends; any still open when the cancellation applies is canceled. It cancels open orders, including those that triggers placed (TWAP slices, ladder levels and exit orders). By default it does not cancel triggers: standalone stop-loss, take-profit and trailing triggers and TWAPs keep running and can place new orders; a ladder stops once its levels are canceled. An attached stop-loss, take-profit or trailing leg whose exit order is canceled ends, and so do the parent's other legs when oco is set, so the position loses that protection. Other attached legs keep protecting the parent's filled quantity; those of a parent canceled before any fill end with it. Set include_triggers to also stop every matching trigger, attached legs included, in the same request; matched_triggers counts them. Every request counts 10 against the cancel rate limit, however many orders it cancels, a dry run and a retry included.

400.description: An invalid or refused request: a malformed body (BAD_REQUEST) or a refused field or order; code names the reason, and violations name the refused field.

413.description: REQUEST_TOO_LARGE: the request body is over the 256 KiB limit; nothing was done.

post.description: Set or disable a dead-man switch timeout for automatic cancel-all. Supports optional symbol and side scope with idempotent heartbeat refresh. On expiry it cancels open orders in scope, including those that triggers placed (TWAP slices, ladder levels and exit orders). By default it does not cancel triggers: standalone stop-loss, take-profit and trailing triggers and TWAPs keep running and can place new orders; a ladder stops once its levels are canceled. An attached stop-loss, take-profit or trailing leg whose exit order is canceled ends, and so do the parent's other legs when oco is set, so the position loses that protection. Other attached legs keep protecting the parent's filled quantity; those of a parent canceled before any fill end with it. Set include_triggers to also stop every matching trigger, attached legs included, when the switch fires.

400.description: An invalid or refused request: a malformed body (BAD_REQUEST) or a refused field or order; code names the reason, and violations name the refused field.

413.description: REQUEST_TOO_LARGE: the request body is over the 256 KiB limit; nothing was done.

post.description: Cancel up to 50 orders by order ID or client order ID in one request. post.description: Cancel all of the account's triggers that match an optional list of symbols, a side and a list of trigger types in one request, with a dry-run count. It cancels no order of its own: every matching trigger created before the requestId was first accepted ends canceled with reason CANCEL_ALL, releases its reserved funds and places no order after the response, and its open orders are canceled with it as Cancel Trigger cancels them (a TWAP's working slice, a ladder's open levels, an attached leg's working exit). An order a stop already placed stays open, and a trigger created later keeps running. An order's attached take-profit, stop-loss and trailing legs end together, and so do an OCO's two legs, when any of them matches. Every request counts 10 against the cancel rate limit, however many triggers match, a dry run and a retry included. A retry with the same requestId and criteria within 2 minutes returns the original count and cancels nothing again.

400.description: An invalid or refused request: a malformed body (BAD_REQUEST) or a refused field or trigger; code names the reason, and violations name the refused field.

413.description: REQUEST_TOO_LARGE: the request body is over the 256 KiB limit; nothing was done.

post.description: Cancel up to 50 triggers by trigger ID in one request. Returns per-trigger accept or reject results in request order with aggregate counts. post.description: Create a one-cancels-the-other order list: a take-profit and a stop-loss over a quantity the account already holds. The quantity is reserved once for both legs. When one leg's order trades the whole quantity, the other is canceled; a partly filled order's rest stays protected by the other leg. Cancel All Orders and the dead-man switch do not cancel OCOs; an OCO leg's working order they cancel cancels the OCO.
